title: Neuron-enriched STAT4 shapes time- and context-dependent neuronal outcomes in Alzheimer’s disease
title_zh: 神经元富集的 STAT4 在阿尔茨海默病中塑造时间与环境依赖的神经元结局
abstract: Abstract Background Neuronal dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is increasingly linked to dynamic and context-dependent alterations in intracellular signaling. However, how these changes drive progressive neurodegeneration and divergent neuronal outcomes remains poorly understood. Methods Integrative analyses across independent human single-nucleus RNA sequencing datasets were performed to identify neuronal factors consistently altered in AD. Signal transducer and activator of transcription 4 (STAT4) distribution in different cell types was further validated using a mouse single-cell RNA sequencing dataset and experimental models. Functions of STAT4 were examined in human SH-SY5Y cells, mouse HT22 neuronal cells, mouse primary neurons, and inducible systems. In vivo effects were assessed in 3×Tg-AD and wild-type mice with AAV-mediated Stat4 modulation and pharmacological ERK inhibition. Multi-omics approaches, including RNA-seq, Cut&Tag, and RIP-seq, were used to explore downstream regulatory mechanisms. Results Integrative analyses identified STAT4 as a neuron-enriched factor consistently reduced in AD neurons. STAT4 supported neuronal integrity and synaptic homeostasis under basal conditions. Inducible restoration of STAT4 expression exerted divergent effects in a time-dependent manner, with early adaptive responses transitioning to later oxidative stress- and apoptosis-associated changes. Sustained STAT4 restoration induced oxidative stress, apoptosis-related signaling, and tau protein-related alterations, which were attenuated by ERK inhibition. In contrast, the beneficial outputs, including reduced Aβ burden and improved synaptic and neuronal markers, were preserved despite ERK inhibition. Parallel analyses in wild-type mice showed a delayed trajectory, indicating disease-context-dependent modulation. STAT4 was further associated with coordinated signaling networks and hnRNPK-related regulatory complexes. Conclusions These findings define a time- and context-dependent signaling framework in which STAT4-associated outputs progressively shift toward maladaptive, ERK-sensitive responses in AD. Selective constraint of the late-stage signaling imbalance may attenuate the pathological outcomes while preserving the beneficial effects, providing a potential strategy for context-specific therapeutic intervention.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 阿尔茨海默病（AD）中神经元功能障碍日益与细胞内信号传导的动态、环境依赖性改变相关联。然而，这些改变如何驱动进行性神经退化和分歧性神经元结局仍不甚清楚。方法 对独立人类单核 RNA 测序数据集进行整合分析，以鉴定在 AD 中持续改变的神经元因子。使用小鼠单细胞 RNA 测序数据集和实验模型进一步验证了信号转导和转录激活因子 4（STAT4）在不同细胞类型中的分布。在人类 SH-SY5Y 细胞、小鼠 HT22 神经元细胞、小鼠原代神经元和诱导系统中考察了 STAT4 的功能。在 3×Tg-AD 和野生型小鼠中通过腺相关病毒介导的 Stat4 调节和药理 ERK 抑制评估体内效应。采用包括 RNA-seq、Cut&Tag 和 RIP-seq 在内的多组学方法探索下游调控机制。结果 整合分析鉴定出 STAT4 是一种在 AD 神经元中持续降低的神经元富集因子。STAT4 在基础条件下支持神经元完整性和突触稳态。STAT4 表达的诱导性恢复以时间依赖方式产生分歧性效应，早期适应性反应转向随后与氧化应激和凋亡相关的变化。持续的 STAT4 恢复诱导氧化应激、凋亡相关信号和与 tau 蛋白相关的改变，这些可通过 ERK 抑制剂减弱。相反，包括减少 Aβ 负担和改善突触及神经元标志物在内的有益输出在 ERK 抑制下得以保留。野生型小鼠的平行分析显示延迟轨迹，表明存在疾病环境依赖的调节。STAT4 进一步与协调的信号网络和异质核糖核蛋白 K 相关的调控复合体相关。结论 这些发现定义了一个时间与环境依赖的信号框架，其中与 STAT4 相关的输出在 AD 中逐渐转向对 ERK 敏感的不适应性反应。选择性约束晚期信号失衡可能减轻病理结局，同时保留有益效应，为情境特异性治疗干预提供潜在策略。
